evidence.paraphrase: An unnamed Brahmin sage of the Āṅgirasa family has Bharata as son. Fearful of attachment even in this birth, Bharata meditates on Gaṇeśa near the sage. Hearing Vedic and other Gaṇeśa praise strengthens previous knowledge. He conceals all cleverness, displaying dull childlike conduct out of fear of marriage and attachment. The father is an unnamed Āṅgirasa descendant, not the creator sage Aṅgiras himself.
evidence.verifier: Mudgala continuation6 author, direct Sanskrit body
evidence.verification_notes: Read actual cited body; attributed dialogue kept distinct from narrator fact. Independent root review pending.

evidence.paraphrase: Father gives Bharata sacred thread and teaches sandhyā, cleanliness and Vedic acts including ācamana. Bharata does not accept instruction, acts differently even when struck, performs acts when physically guided but later appears unable to recall them. People call him Jaḍa and doubt his knowledge; he disregards honor, insult, blame and praise. Father does not arrange marriage because of apparent dullness, which pleases Bharata.
evidence.verifier: Mudgala continuation6 author, direct Sanskrit body
evidence.verification_notes: Read actual cited body; attributed dialogue kept distinct from narrator fact. Independent root review pending.

evidence.paraphrase: Father dies in time; unnamed virtuous mother follows him (sahagā). Nine brothers born to his mother’s co-wife take control over Bharata: these are half-brothers in this later birth, not Ṛṣabha’s earlier sons. Their arrogant wives give leftovers, spoiled or burnt food and husks without affection. Brothers dishonor him with words/clothes and call him family disgrace. He eats rejected food as nectar wearing rags; when women withhold even that, he eats only once within two or three days. This is deprivation, not a fasting vow.
evidence.verifier: Mudgala continuation6 author, direct Sanskrit body
evidence.verification_notes: Read actual cited body; attributed dialogue kept distinct from narrator fact. Independent root review pending.

evidence.paraphrase: Hungry Bharata wanders house to house seeking food and accepts work. Pleased people give food/clothes; his brothers see him, bring him back and make him their worker. Their wives still give bad food/husks, which he eats as nectar. Brothers station him to guard ripe grain fields day and night for food; understanding bodily life, he remains equal in pleasure and pain.
evidence.verifier: Mudgala continuation6 author, direct Sanskrit body
evidence.verification_notes: Read actual cited body; attributed dialogue kept distinct from narrator fact. Independent root review pending.

evidence.paraphrase: Robber chief praises Bhadrakālī and promises a human victim if he obtains abundant wealth. Wealth is then actually obtained; source does not explicitly narrate a deity boon or identify its grantor. He sends robbers at night; they happen upon Bharata, seize him by force and take him to their station. Bharata understands bodily prārabdha. Chief honors and feeds him tasty food, then takes him with music to the goddess.
evidence.verifier: Mudgala continuation6 author, direct Sanskrit body
evidence.verification_notes: Read actual cited body; attributed dialogue kept distinct from narrator fact. Independent root review pending.

evidence.paraphrase: After Mahākālī worship the chief draws a naked sword to kill Bharata. Seeing possible bodily death, Bharata is unshaken and remembers Gaṇapati, accepting whether body falls today or lives long. Angry Gaṇapatya Mahākālī emerges from the image, takes the chief’s sword from his hand, beheads him with it and drinks blood. Other robbers are killed with that sword. Goddess plays with her own gaṇas while intent on Gaṇeśa praise. Bharata bows and leaves, wandering freely for alms while remembering Gaṇapati. No actual liberation narrated.
evidence.verifier: Mudgala continuation6 author, direct Sanskrit body
evidence.verification_notes: Read actual cited body; attributed dialogue kept distinct from narrator fact. Independent root review pending.

evidence.paraphrase: Sindhu ruler Rahūgaṇa is inwardly inclined through prior saṃskāra but cannot gain peace despite effort. He goes toward Kapila’s āśrama near Gaṅgā, said by a Brahmin to be on Gautamī’s south bank. His palanquin bearers tire; attendants recruit replacements, finding the Āṅgirasa sage Bharata. Accepting bodily prārabdha he carries without distress. To avoid injuring creatures he steps only where none are present, slowing bearers and rocking the palanquin, distressing king. Gaṅgā/Gautamī labels preserved as this witness’s setting, not mapped to modern geography.
evidence.verifier: Mudgala continuation6 author, direct Sanskrit body
evidence.verification_notes: Read actual cited body; attributed dialogue kept distinct from narrator fact. Independent root review pending.

evidence.paraphrase: Angry Rahūgaṇa orders steady carrying; fearful bearers blame newcomer as moving like drunk. King rebukes him as wicked/mad. Knowing king desires yoga and is qualified, Bharata replies that all is māyā/delusion/untrue, questions king/people division, says he has abandoned duality/equality and king cannot discipline him into abandoning yoga. He resumes silently carrying and worshipping Gaṇapati. Hearing yogic speech, frightened king jumps to ground, sees ragged Brahmin with sacred thread/Brahman radiance, prostrates and addresses him respectfully.
evidence.verifier: Mudgala continuation6 author, direct Sanskrit body
evidence.verification_notes: Read actual cited body; attributed dialogue kept distinct from narrator fact. Independent root review pending.

evidence.paraphrase: Rahūgaṇa asks pardon for ignorant offense, sees apparent avadhūta with sacred thread, and asks whether he is Kapila, Nārada, Aṅgirā, Pulaha, Kratu, Datta or Yājñavalkya. These are queried identities, not actual identifications of Bharata or onstage visits by those sages.
evidence.verifier: Mudgala continuation6 author, direct Sanskrit body
evidence.verification_notes: Read actual cited body; attributed dialogue kept distinct from narrator fact. Independent root review pending.

evidence.paraphrase: Rahūgaṇa explains fear of offending Brahmins: he praises them as Supreme Lord’s bodies, supports of acts/knowledge/Brahman, the printed25 mouth/hearing/gods-stomach clause is separately unresolved; gifts yield imperishable state, mantras/gods depend on them and mantra-less acts are fruitless. He calls devoted act/tapas/knowledge/yoga Brahmins liberators/teachers/Brahman. He attributes divine falls to slighting/curses, restoration to Brahmins and all attainment to service. He fears them more than Viṣṇu/Śiva. Taking Bharata’s feet, bowing with head there, he cries; compassionate Bharata raises him and begins reply. These claims are king’s praise, not universal physical/social facts or new narrated curses.
evidence.verifier: Mudgala continuation6 author, direct Sanskrit body
evidence.verification_notes: Read actual cited body; attributed dialogue kept distinct from narrator fact. Independent root review pending.

evidence.paraphrase: Printed yacchrutam refers to what is heard through Brahmin mouth arriving in gods’ stomachs. Exact semantics are unresolved; do not silently emend to yahutam or assert conveyed offerings.

evidence.paraphrase: Bharata identifies himself as Āṅgirasa, called Jaḍa Bharata, formerly Svāyambhuva Bharata and now Jaḍa. He assures Rahūgaṇa that ignorant insult to his body will not produce sin, he need not fear and may go; Bharata will go freely under prārabdha. This is forgiveness of this offense, not a generic future immunity. Rahūgaṇa praises meeting, identifies Sindhu kingship, says he left royal matters to seek peace from Kapila at Gautamī, and asks Bharata to accept him as disciple and teach peace. Compassionate Bharata begins difficult Vedic-secret yoga-peace instruction.
evidence.verifier: Mudgala continuation6 author, direct Sanskrit body
evidence.verification_notes: Read actual cited body; attributed dialogue kept distinct from narrator fact. Independent root review pending.

evidence.paraphrase: Bharata teaches fourfold body and fourfold embodied self appear different through delusion despite unity. Body-Brahman is bindu, embodied-self Brahman soham; union is bodha/self-arising Brahman varied by vikalpa. When bodha ceases, Sāṅkhya Brahman enjoys only own happiness; he questions own happiness without other happiness and describes other-arising and its seed. Beyond self/other arising, Svānanda is union/nondifference. No remembered four-body names supplied.
evidence.verifier: Mudgala continuation6 author, direct Sanskrit body
evidence.verification_notes: Read actual cited body; attributed dialogue kept distinct from narrator fact. Independent root review pending.

evidence.paraphrase: 18 states fivefold Svānanda and names satya/asatya/sama/neti fourth; 19–20 relate self/other arising, experience and varied Brahmans/worlds.21 names name/form as asatya/Śākta Brahman; 22 gives divided name/form and immortal solar self/all-illumining Brahman. Precise reference/allocation of experience in19 and name/form versus solar self in22 withheld; literal distinctions retained without remembered philosophical repair.
evidence.verifier: Mudgala continuation6 author, direct Sanskrit body
evidence.verification_notes: Meaning-bearing philosophical referents unresolved; teaching spine/chapter21 PARTIAL.

evidence.paraphrase: Bharata teaches Viṣṇu as bliss/nondifference/equality of two and being/nonbeing; Śiva fourth, neti, unmanifest, delusion-free independent Brahman. Fourfold union is own-form māyā-associated Vināyaka; ayoga destroys union and is māyā-free Gaṇeśa. Ayoga brings withdrawal/beyond own distinction; yoga-peace does not perceive either union or ayoga. Māyā-associated versus free distinctions are delusion to abandon. Mind fivefold and sovereignty constitute twofold delusion; relinquish them to become peaceful. All statements remain attributed teaching.
evidence.verifier: Mudgala continuation6 author, direct Sanskrit body
evidence.verification_notes: Read actual cited body; attributed dialogue kept distinct from narrator fact. Independent root review pending.

evidence.paraphrase: Bharata stops; king bows, abandons kingdom and goes forest. Practicing prescribed means, Rahūgaṇa actually gains peace and becomes Gaṇapatya. No new apparition or deity boon scene in these verses.
evidence.verifier: Mudgala continuation6 author, direct Sanskrit body
evidence.verification_notes: Read actual cited body; attributed dialogue kept distinct from narrator fact. Independent root review pending.

evidence.paraphrase: Āṅgirasa Bharata wanders Earth, arrives by fate at Mayūreśa field, recognizes previous Gaṇeśa manifestation and stays meditating in one place as if dull. After one year Gaṇeśa actually comes to see him, mounted on mouse and accompanied by Siddhi/Buddhi. Bharata bows and hymns with tears/gooseflesh and devotion. The one-year interval belongs to this field arrival/meditation, not all prior lives.
evidence.verifier: Mudgala continuation6 author, direct Sanskrit body
evidence.verification_notes: Read actual cited body; attributed dialogue kept distinct from narrator fact. Independent root review pending.

evidence.paraphrase: Bharata hymns peace-form/giver, Vighneśa/Heramba, Siddhi/Buddhi lord and giver, devotee-fear remover, devotion-loving/yoga-peace Gaṇeśa, mouse-mounted/four-armed/Svānanda/Vakratunda, infinite forms/play. He is fulfilled by sight inaccessible even in Vedic reach, says devotion alone drew deity to him, and asks what gift can please the source of all portions. Four arms and Vakratunda here are hymn attributes, distinct from narrator’s actual mouse/Siddhi/Buddhi appearance.
evidence.verifier: Mudgala continuation6 author, direct Sanskrit body

evidence.paraphrase: Bharata offers his body, bows and requests ONLY firm unwavering devotion to deity’s feet. Repeatedly bowing, he dances with love. Gaṇeśa grants firm unwavering devotion; hymn will give yoga-peace and please him. Whatever a reciter desires he will give, and hearers obtain likewise. God disappears; Bharata remains devoted there. Neither requested liberation nor a new bodily transformation boon is added.
evidence.verifier: Mudgala continuation6 author, direct Sanskrit body

evidence.paraphrase: At the end Bharata actually becomes Gaṇeśa-form. Narrator locates the famous sage’s cave/place north of Gaṇeśa and facing him at one krośa. People who see that place attain permanent liberation. Devoted hearers/readers of Bharata account obtain enjoyment/liberation. Mudgala closes Priyavrata-family righteous kings devoted to various gods. Site not assigned a modern location; site-view benefit not retroactively substituted for king’s actual outcome.

evidence.paraphrase: Svāyambhuva Manu’s son Uttānapāda righteously rules Madhyadeśa. Wives are Sunīti and Suruci; Dhruva is Sunīti’s son, Uttama Suruci’s son. King is controlled/deluded by Suruci and disregards Sunīti. Dhruva approaches to sit on royal lap, is dishonored with Suruci’s malicious involvement, and goes angrily to forest. He meets/bows to Nārada, who learns events and gives Viṣṇu’s twelve-syllable mantra. At Mathurā he meditates and performs severe tapas for ONE THOUSAND YEARS. Pleased Viṣṇu comes and gives undivided earthly kingship and, at end, heavenly kingship/Viṣṇu’s Dhruva-form abode. No recalled six-month duration or exact bīja imported.
evidence.verifier: Mudgala continuation6 author, direct Sanskrit body
evidence.verification_notes: Read actual cited body; attributed dialogue kept distinct from narrator fact. Independent root review pending.

evidence.paraphrase: Dhruva returns and bows to parents; king honors his radiance, later makes him king and goes forest for tapas. Gaṇeśa-devoted Nārada teaches him to worship Gaṇeśa beyond difference/nondifference, as gods, sages/yogins and earlier kings do, for peace. Nārada gives SIX-SYLLABLE mantra; its power makes Uttānapāda Gaṇapatya. Remembering Gaṇanātha at death, he actually attains Gaṇanātha sāyujya. This six-syllable initiation belongs to father, distinct from Dhruva’s later one-syllable Gaṇeśa mantra.
evidence.verifier: Mudgala continuation6 author, direct Sanskrit body
evidence.verification_notes: Read actual cited body; attributed dialogue kept distinct from narrator fact. Independent root review pending.

evidence.paraphrase: Nārada visits ruling Dhruva, who honors his guru. He says Viṣṇu sent him from Vikuṇṭha to direct prescribed Mayūreśa pilgrimage for lasting abode, otherwise obstacle/fall. First-person m adīyakam in23 belongs to relayed Viṣṇu promise, not Nārada’s own new abode grant. Viṣṇu also instructs one-syllable Gaṇeśa japa:when Dhruva abode dissolves at Brahmā-day end, Dhruva will attain peace/Brahman; without it yoga-peace cannot come. Nārada properly gives ONE-SYLLABLE mantra; Dhruva becomes siddha, goes Mayūreśa and performs pilgrimage with gateway marks. Prediction of end-stage kept separate from actual ending32–33.
evidence.verifier: Mudgala continuation6 author, direct Sanskrit body

evidence.paraphrase: Dhruva returns city, rules, and at end goes heavenly Dhruva abode supporting luminaries. Meditating on Gaṇapati there, when Dhruva station perishes he actually goes straight to Svānanda. Humans seeing Dhruvavināyaka there or hearing this Dhruva account gain enjoyment and firm liberation. Actual station/Svānanda ending is distinct from earlier Viṣṇu promise.

evidence.paraphrase: Aṅga, a descendant in Dhruva’s line, righteously protects people like father. His wife is Mṛtyu’s UNNAMED daughter; their son Vena is cruel. Exhausted by failed instruction, Aṅga abandons kingdom and goes forest sorrowfully. Robbers plunder rulerless land; frightened people seek Brahmins, who enthrone Vena in paternal realm. He kills robbers but abandons proper conduct, hurting varṇa/āśrama practitioners. Sages restrain him; he claims everyone should worship him as protector. Angry Brahmins kill him by curse.
evidence.verifier: Mudgala continuation6 author, direct Sanskrit body
evidence.verification_notes: Read actual cited body; attributed dialogue kept distinct from narrator fact. Independent root review pending.

evidence.paraphrase: Sages churn Vena’s LEFT aṅga/body-part seeking king; cruel sin-formed man arises, short, dusky, bearded and tawny-eyed. They say niṣīda; he becomes named Niṣāda, receives forest station and Niṣādas descend from him. They then churn RIGHT aṅga; an energetic COUPLE emerges, both Viṣṇu-kalā-associated. Couple bows to Brahmins; male is consecrated king and named Pṛthu, upholding royal dharma/prosperity. Neither left thigh/right arm specificity nor partner name Arci is supplied.
evidence.verifier: Mudgala continuation6 author, direct Sanskrit body
evidence.verification_notes: Read actual cited body; attributed dialogue kept distinct from narrator fact. Independent root review pending.

evidence.paraphrase: After time people lack food and seek Pṛthu. Earth swallowed resources under Vena’s adharma and cannot return them under righteous king. Angry Pṛthu draws bow/arrow to kill Earth; she flees in cow form and he pursues like Yama. Finding no refuge, she seeks Pṛthu with folded hands, asks him not to kill woman/cow/Earth and protect surrendered one. He threatens death unless she manifests varied food always. Earth says plants already consumed cannot be directly returned; asks first leveling, then calf and milker so cow-form yields all plants as milk. Killing would be futile without these arrangements.
evidence.verifier: Mudgala continuation6 author, direct Sanskrit body
evidence.verification_notes: Read actual cited body; attributed dialogue kept distinct from narrator fact. Independent root review pending.

evidence.paraphrase: Pṛthu crushes mountains with bow-tip, levels Earth and arranges towns/villages; source says this starts their arrangement. He makes Earth his DAUGHTER by adoption/putrītva, so she is called Pṛthvī. With Manu as CALF, Pṛthu himself MILKS six-taste food-milk. Beings of three worlds then obtain their own food-milk. Adoption and calf-role are not biological parentage.
evidence.verifier: Mudgala continuation6 author, direct Sanskrit body
evidence.verification_notes: Read actual cited body; attributed dialogue kept distinct from narrator fact. Independent root review pending.

evidence.paraphrase: Milking roles: Veda-form Brahmā CALF/Bṛhaspati MILKER takes milk; 36 does not separately name its substance. Rudra CALF/Kālāgnirudra MILKER yields flesh-form Hara-life milk. Viṣṇu CALF/Yajamāna MILKER yields act-born sacrifice-support milk. Sun CALF/Dhruva MILKER yields luminaries’ life. Śeṣa CALF/Vāsuki MILKER yields serpent food. Śiva CALF/Nandikeśvara MILKER yields knowledge/vidyā milk. These are source-specific cosmic milking roles, not parents/children; Rudra and Śiva labels retained separately in this table.
evidence.verifier: Mudgala continuation6 author, direct Sanskrit body

evidence.paraphrase: Mobile/immobile beings and lords milk Pṛthu-prepared Earth. He honors and joyfully protects her as daughter; she remains happy. He rules Earth as emperor and undertakes hundred horse sacrifices with great dakṣiṇā. Brahmā, Viṣṇu, Śaṅkara, Indra-led gods, Gandharvas, Kaśyapa-led sages, Śeṣa-led Nāgas and varied people with wives come. Hundred opening count is kept distinct from final NINETY-NINE completion at52.

evidence.paraphrase: As last sacrifice begins, worried Indra in matted hair/rags steals horse. Pṛthu’s UNNAMED son sees him but lets him go as ascetic; Indra leaves horse and disappears afraid. Next he uses bone-bearing/ash-smeared disguise and son does not strike him. Altogether Indra steals horse SIX TIMES. Pṛthu prepares to kill him; Brahmā consoles/restrains him, and Indra is not killed. Pṛthu completes NINETY-NINE sacrifices. Urged by Brahmā, Indra bows; Pṛthu renounces enmity and embraces him. Honored gods/guests depart; Pṛthu resumes righteous protection.
evidence.verifier: Mudgala continuation6 author, direct Sanskrit body

assertions.value: Hides cleverness and displays dullness to avoid marriage/attachment; hearing Gaṇeśa praise strengthens prior knowledge.
Jaḍa, given by people for apparent dullness; not actual loss of his concealed knowledge.
Father does not arrange marriage because of apparent dullness; Bharata is pleased.
Father dies; mother follows him, described as sahagā. No mother proper name supplied.
Rejected/burnt food and husks, rags, insults; after withholding, one eating occasion in two or three days, not a voluntary vow.
If abundant wealth obtained, offer a human victim; actual receipt follows, with no explicit deity-grant dialogue.
Bhadrakālī at27; Mahākālī at33/36, explicitly Gaṇapatya at36.
Avoids creatures with each step, causing slower movement and palanquin rocking; king suffers.
Māyā/delusion/untrue world; rejects king/people division and abandoning yoga through royal discipline; equal beyond duality.
Brahmins as divine bodies/teachers/Brahman and supports of acts/knowledge/mantras; gifts/service benefits and curse/slighting dangers.

narrative_events.details: An unnamed Brahmin sage of the Āṅgirasa family has Bharata as son. Fearful of attachment even in this birth, Bharata meditates on Gaṇeśa near the sage. Hearing Vedic and other Gaṇeśa praise strengthens previous knowledge. He conceals all cleverness, displaying dull childlike conduct out of fear of marriage and attachment. The father is an unnamed Āṅgirasa descendant, not the creator sage Aṅgiras himself.

Father gives Bharata sacred thread and teaches sandhyā, cleanliness and Vedic acts including ācamana. Bharata does not accept instruction, acts differently even when struck, performs acts when physically guided but later appears unable to recall them. People call him Jaḍa and doubt his knowledge; he disregards honor, insult, blame and praise. Father does not arrange marriage because of apparent dullness, which pleases Bharata.

Father dies in time; unnamed virtuous mother follows him (sahagā). Nine brothers born to his mother’s co-wife take control over Bharata: these are half-brothers in this later birth, not Ṛṣabha’s earlier sons. Their arrogant wives give leftovers, spoiled or burnt food and husks without affection. Brothers dishonor him with words/clothes and call him family disgrace. He eats rejected food as nectar wearing rags; when women withhold even that, he eats only once within two or three days. This is deprivation, not a fasting vow.

Hungry Bharata wanders house to house seeking food and accepts work. Pleased people give food/clothes; his brothers see him, bring him back and make him their worker. Their wives still give bad food/husks, which he eats as nectar. Brothers station him to guard ripe grain fields day and night for food; understanding bodily life, he remains equal in pleasure and pain.

Robber chief praises Bhadrakālī and promises a human victim if he obtains abundant wealth. Wealth is then actually obtained; source does not explicitly narrate a deity boon or identify its grantor. He sends robbers at night; they happen upon Bharata, seize him by force and take him to their station. Bharata understands bodily prārabdha. Chief honors and feeds him tasty food, then takes him with music to the goddess.

After Mahākālī worship the chief draws a naked sword to kill Bharata. Seeing possible bodily death, Bharata is unshaken and remembers Gaṇapati, accepting whether body falls today or lives long. Angry Gaṇapatya Mahākālī emerges from the image, takes the chief’s sword from his hand, beheads him with it and drinks blood. Other robbers are killed with that sword. Goddess plays with her own gaṇas while intent on Gaṇeśa praise. Bharata bows and leaves, wandering freely for alms while remembering Gaṇapati. No actual liberation narrated.
narrative_events.outcome: Chief and robbers killed; Bharata bows and resumes alms-wandering/Gaṇeśa remembrance.

narrative_events.details: Sindhu ruler Rahūgaṇa is inwardly inclined through prior saṃskāra but cannot gain peace despite effort. He goes toward Kapila’s āśrama near Gaṅgā, said by a Brahmin to be on Gautamī’s south bank. His palanquin bearers tire; attendants recruit replacements, finding the Āṅgirasa sage Bharata. Accepting bodily prārabdha he carries without distress. To avoid injuring creatures he steps only where none are present, slowing bearers and rocking the palanquin, distressing king. Gaṅgā/Gautamī labels preserved as this witness’s setting, not mapped to modern geography.

Angry Rahūgaṇa orders steady carrying; fearful bearers blame newcomer as moving like drunk. King rebukes him as wicked/mad. Knowing king desires yoga and is qualified, Bharata replies that all is māyā/delusion/untrue, questions king/people division, says he has abandoned duality/equality and king cannot discipline him into abandoning yoga. He resumes silently carrying and worshipping Gaṇapati. Hearing yogic speech, frightened king jumps to ground, sees ragged Brahmin with sacred thread/Brahman radiance, prostrates and addresses him respectfully.

Rahūgaṇa asks pardon for ignorant offense, sees apparent avadhūta with sacred thread, and asks whether he is Kapila, Nārada, Aṅgirā, Pulaha, Kratu, Datta or Yājñavalkya. These are queried identities, not actual identifications of Bharata or onstage visits by those sages.

Rahūgaṇa explains fear of offending Brahmins: he praises them as Supreme Lord’s bodies, supports of acts/knowledge/Brahman, the printed25 mouth/hearing/gods-stomach clause is separately unresolved; gifts yield imperishable state, mantras/gods depend on them and mantra-less acts are fruitless. He calls devoted act/tapas/knowledge/yoga Brahmins liberators/teachers/Brahman. He attributes divine falls to slighting/curses, restoration to Brahmins and all attainment to service. He fears them more than Viṣṇu/Śiva. Taking Bharata’s feet, bowing with head there, he cries; compassionate Bharata raises him and begins reply. These claims are king’s praise, not universal physical/social facts or new narrated curses.
narrative_events.outcome: King cries at Bharata’s feet; compassionate sage raises him.

narrative_events.details: Bharata identifies himself as Āṅgirasa, called Jaḍa Bharata, formerly Svāyambhuva Bharata and now Jaḍa. He assures Rahūgaṇa that ignorant insult to his body will not produce sin, he need not fear and may go; Bharata will go freely under prārabdha. This is forgiveness of this offense, not a generic future immunity. Rahūgaṇa praises meeting, identifies Sindhu kingship, says he left royal matters to seek peace from Kapila at Gautamī, and asks Bharata to accept him as disciple and teach peace. Compassionate Bharata begins difficult Vedic-secret yoga-peace instruction.

Bharata teaches fourfold body and fourfold embodied self appear different through delusion despite unity. Body-Brahman is bindu, embodied-self Brahman soham; union is bodha/self-arising Brahman varied by vikalpa. When bodha ceases, Sāṅkhya Brahman enjoys only own happiness; he questions own happiness without other happiness and describes other-arising and its seed. Beyond self/other arising, Svānanda is union/nondifference. No remembered four-body names supplied.

18 states fivefold Svānanda and names satya/asatya/sama/neti fourth; 19–20 relate self/other arising, experience and varied Brahmans/worlds.21 names name/form as asatya/Śākta Brahman; 22 gives divided name/form and immortal solar self/all-illumining Brahman. Precise reference/allocation of experience in19 and name/form versus solar self in22 withheld; literal distinctions retained without remembered philosophical repair.

Bharata teaches Viṣṇu as bliss/nondifference/equality of two and being/nonbeing; Śiva fourth, neti, unmanifest, delusion-free independent Brahman. Fourfold union is own-form māyā-associated Vināyaka; ayoga destroys union and is māyā-free Gaṇeśa. Ayoga brings withdrawal/beyond own distinction; yoga-peace does not perceive either union or ayoga. Māyā-associated versus free distinctions are delusion to abandon. Mind fivefold and sovereignty constitute twofold delusion; relinquish them to become peaceful. All statements remain attributed teaching.
Bharata stops; king bows, abandons kingdom and goes forest. Practicing prescribed means, Rahūgaṇa actually gains peace and becomes Gaṇapatya. No new apparition or deity boon scene in these verses.
narrative_events.outcome: Rahūgaṇa actually attains peace and becomes Gaṇapatya.

narrative_events.details: Āṅgirasa Bharata wanders Earth, arrives by fate at Mayūreśa field, recognizes previous Gaṇeśa manifestation and stays meditating in one place as if dull. After one year Gaṇeśa actually comes to see him, mounted on mouse and accompanied by Siddhi/Buddhi. Bharata bows and hymns with tears/gooseflesh and devotion. The one-year interval belongs to this field arrival/meditation, not all prior lives.

Bharata hymns peace-form/giver, Vighneśa/Heramba, Siddhi/Buddhi lord and giver, devotee-fear remover, devotion-loving/yoga-peace Gaṇeśa, mouse-mounted/four-armed/Svānanda/Vakratunda, infinite forms/play. He is fulfilled by sight inaccessible even in Vedic reach, says devotion alone drew deity to him, and asks what gift can please the source of all portions. Four arms and Vakratunda here are hymn attributes, distinct from narrator’s actual mouse/Siddhi/Buddhi appearance.

Bharata offers his body, bows and requests ONLY firm unwavering devotion to deity’s feet. Repeatedly bowing, he dances with love. Gaṇeśa grants firm unwavering devotion; hymn will give yoga-peace and please him. Whatever a reciter desires he will give, and hearers obtain likewise. God disappears; Bharata remains devoted there. Neither requested liberation nor a new bodily transformation boon is added.
narrative_events.outcome: Firm devotion granted; deity disappears and Bharata remains there.

narrative_events.details: At the end Bharata actually becomes Gaṇeśa-form. Narrator locates the famous sage’s cave/place north of Gaṇeśa and facing him at one krośa. People who see that place attain permanent liberation. Devoted hearers/readers of Bharata account obtain enjoyment/liberation. Mudgala closes Priyavrata-family righteous kings devoted to various gods. Site not assigned a modern location; site-view benefit not retroactively substituted for king’s actual outcome.
narrative_events.outcome: Bharata becomes Gaṇeśa-form; site position and separate audience benefits stated.

narrative_events.details: Svāyambhuva Manu’s son Uttānapāda righteously rules Madhyadeśa. Wives are Sunīti and Suruci; Dhruva is Sunīti’s son, Uttama Suruci’s son. King is controlled/deluded by Suruci and disregards Sunīti. Dhruva approaches to sit on royal lap, is dishonored with Suruci’s malicious involvement, and goes angrily to forest. He meets/bows to Nārada, who learns events and gives Viṣṇu’s twelve-syllable mantra. At Mathurā he meditates and performs severe tapas for ONE THOUSAND YEARS. Pleased Viṣṇu comes and gives undivided earthly kingship and, at end, heavenly kingship/Viṣṇu’s Dhruva-form abode. No recalled six-month duration or exact bīja imported.

Dhruva returns and bows to parents; king honors his radiance, later makes him king and goes forest for tapas. Gaṇeśa-devoted Nārada teaches him to worship Gaṇeśa beyond difference/nondifference, as gods, sages/yogins and earlier kings do, for peace. Nārada gives SIX-SYLLABLE mantra; its power makes Uttānapāda Gaṇapatya. Remembering Gaṇanātha at death, he actually attains Gaṇanātha sāyujya. This six-syllable initiation belongs to father, distinct from Dhruva’s later one-syllable Gaṇeśa mantra.
narrative_events.outcome: Father’s actual Gaṇeśa sāyujya; Dhruva rules.

narrative_events.details: Nārada visits ruling Dhruva, who honors his guru. He says Viṣṇu sent him from Vikuṇṭha to direct prescribed Mayūreśa pilgrimage for lasting abode, otherwise obstacle/fall. First-person m adīyakam in23 belongs to relayed Viṣṇu promise, not Nārada’s own new abode grant. Viṣṇu also instructs one-syllable Gaṇeśa japa:when Dhruva abode dissolves at Brahmā-day end, Dhruva will attain peace/Brahman; without it yoga-peace cannot come. Nārada properly gives ONE-SYLLABLE mantra; Dhruva becomes siddha, goes Mayūreśa and performs pilgrimage with gateway marks. Prediction of end-stage kept separate from actual ending32–33.

With mantra-knowing Brahmins Dhruva installs Gaṇeśa, builds extensive costly temple with golden pinnacle and worships devotedly. He names deity Dhruvavināyaka.29 gives half-krośa distance from Gaṇeśa but printed nāpūrvadvārasamīpagam direction clause unresolved.31 residence duration varṣamāsaṃ also not securely normalized.

Dhruva returns city, rules, and at end goes heavenly Dhruva abode supporting luminaries. Meditating on Gaṇapati there, when Dhruva station perishes he actually goes straight to Svānanda. Humans seeing Dhruvavināyaka there or hearing this Dhruva account gain enjoyment and firm liberation. Actual station/Svānanda ending is distinct from earlier Viṣṇu promise.
narrative_events.outcome: Dhruva actually attains Svānanda after luminary-station destruction.

narrative_events.details: Aṅga, a descendant in Dhruva’s line, righteously protects people like father. His wife is Mṛtyu’s UNNAMED daughter; their son Vena is cruel. Exhausted by failed instruction, Aṅga abandons kingdom and goes forest sorrowfully. Robbers plunder rulerless land; frightened people seek Brahmins, who enthrone Vena in paternal realm. He kills robbers but abandons proper conduct, hurting varṇa/āśrama practitioners. Sages restrain him; he claims everyone should worship him as protector. Angry Brahmins kill him by curse.

Sages churn Vena’s LEFT aṅga/body-part seeking king; cruel sin-formed man arises, short, dusky, bearded and tawny-eyed. They say niṣīda; he becomes named Niṣāda, receives forest station and Niṣādas descend from him. They then churn RIGHT aṅga; an energetic COUPLE emerges, both Viṣṇu-kalā-associated. Couple bows to Brahmins; male is consecrated king and named Pṛthu, upholding royal dharma/prosperity. Neither left thigh/right arm specificity nor partner name Arci is supplied.

After time people lack food and seek Pṛthu. Earth swallowed resources under Vena’s adharma and cannot return them under righteous king. Angry Pṛthu draws bow/arrow to kill Earth; she flees in cow form and he pursues like Yama. Finding no refuge, she seeks Pṛthu with folded hands, asks him not to kill woman/cow/Earth and protect surrendered one. He threatens death unless she manifests varied food always. Earth says plants already consumed cannot be directly returned; asks first leveling, then calf and milker so cow-form yields all plants as milk. Killing would be futile without these arrangements.

Pṛthu crushes mountains with bow-tip, levels Earth and arranges towns/villages; source says this starts their arrangement. He makes Earth his DAUGHTER by adoption/putrītva, so she is called Pṛthvī. With Manu as CALF, Pṛthu himself MILKS six-taste food-milk. Beings of three worlds then obtain their own food-milk. Adoption and calf-role are not biological parentage.

Milking roles: Veda-form Brahmā CALF/Bṛhaspati MILKER takes milk; 36 does not separately name its substance. Rudra CALF/Kālāgnirudra MILKER yields flesh-form Hara-life milk. Viṣṇu CALF/Yajamāna MILKER yields act-born sacrifice-support milk. Sun CALF/Dhruva MILKER yields luminaries’ life. Śeṣa CALF/Vāsuki MILKER yields serpent food. Śiva CALF/Nandikeśvara MILKER yields knowledge/vidyā milk. These are source-specific cosmic milking roles, not parents/children; Rudra and Śiva labels retained separately in this table.

Mobile/immobile beings and lords milk Pṛthu-prepared Earth. He honors and joyfully protects her as daughter; she remains happy. He rules Earth as emperor and undertakes hundred horse sacrifices with great dakṣiṇā. Brahmā, Viṣṇu, Śaṅkara, Indra-led gods, Gandharvas, Kaśyapa-led sages, Śeṣa-led Nāgas and varied people with wives come. Hundred opening count is kept distinct from final NINETY-NINE completion at52.

As last sacrifice begins, worried Indra in matted hair/rags steals horse. Pṛthu’s UNNAMED son sees him but lets him go as ascetic; Indra leaves horse and disappears afraid. Next he uses bone-bearing/ash-smeared disguise and son does not strike him. Altogether Indra steals horse SIX TIMES. Pṛthu prepares to kill him; Brahmā consoles/restrains him, and Indra is not killed. Pṛthu completes NINETY-NINE sacrifices. Urged by Brahmā, Indra bows; Pṛthu renounces enmity and embraces him. Honored gods/guests depart; Pṛthu resumes righteous protection.
narrative_events.outcome: 99sacrifices; Indra survives, bows and is embraced; Pṛthu resumes rule.
